**16. Standard commands in the standard menus.** Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select all and Find go in Edit; New, Open, Save, Close and Print in File; show and hide commands in View. Settings and About go where the platform puts them, which `MenuBar` does for you: Tools > Options and Help > About on Windows, the app menu on macOS. Exit on Windows, Quit on macOS. (CMD-2 to CMD-8)
**7. Confirming buttons name the action; never Confirm.** The button that carries out a dialog says what it does. OK appears only on a settings window (Windows) or alone on a message that only informs (macOS). Yes and No appear only together, answering a question that really is yes or no, on Windows. The abandoning button is Cancel; once the work is done it becomes Close. (WRD-7, WRD-8)
**6. Write sentence case; kvit-ui does the rest.** Write every label once, in sentence case: "Select all", "Don't save". On macOS the component turns menu items, buttons, tabs and column headings into title case; on Windows and Linux they stay as written. Never write title case yourself, and never mix the two in one menu. (WRD-6)
# Draft: a section for agent/skills/kvit-ui/SKILL.md

This is a draft for the owner, not yet in the skill. It condenses the wording, symbol, command, menu and shortcut rules of rules.md into what an agent needs while building a screen. Each rule names its rule ids so the reasoning can be looked up.

Assumptions it makes, which change it if decided otherwise:

- Q-3: the app writes every label once, in sentence case, and kvit-ui gives the macOS title case. If both forms are supplied instead, rule 6 changes.
- Q-5, Q-7, Q-11: the Windows forms for OK and Yes/No, the default button and access keys, as recommended in open-questions.md.
- The library changes in library-gaps.md steps 1 to 5 exist (`ui.Form`, `Command`, `MenuBar`, Dialog by form). Until they do, rules 15 to 20 are things the agent does by hand.

The before-and-after pairs come from the survey of kvit-cash, kvit-notes and kvit-works of 2026-10-22 and from kvit-ui's own strings and gallery. The application repositories were not available where this draft was written, so the app pairs are the ones the survey named, with its file:line.

content.content:
### CMD-1

Every command the app has is on a visible command surface (the menu bar, or where the platform allows, a toolbar and its More menu), including ones also on buttons and context menus, never only in a context menu, so every task can be found on screen rather than remembered.

- **Windows:** A menu bar (Kvit-drawn, in the main window) is for an app with many commands in several categories, such as an editing app (Notepad). Another main window may use a toolbar (command bar) with a More menu as its command surface instead. Either way every command is reachable from the menu bar, or from the toolbar and its More menu. Offer each command on as many surfaces as fit: menu bar or toolbar, and the context menu (Q-1).
- **macOS:** Required: the system menu bar, always present.
- **Sources** (33 records, 2 on Microsoft's checklist):
### WIN-16

Settings hold app-wide options people seldom change, and every app setting can be reached from them; everyday commands stay in the working view, options for one view live in that view and options for one document in the File menu; settings that are complex or break things when wrong offer Restore defaults.

- **Windows:** Settings (never Options or Preferences) is a page in the app's window, filling it as one scrolling column rather than a dialog; each change applies at once, with no OK, Cancel or Apply (WIN-23). Its command is the last item of the navigation sidebar, below footer items such as Help; or the last item of the toolbar's More menu, or on the toolbar; with a menu bar and no sidebar, the last item of Tools. About is a section at its bottom (CMD-3). There is no separate Customize command; an object's attributes are its Properties (WIN-17). Every option of a tray app not on its tray menu is in Settings, including Display icon in notification area.
- **macOS:** Settings… in the app menu: a window with a toolbar of panes, changes taking effect at once, no minimise or zoom, titled with the pane's name.
- **Sources** (33 records):

The access-key, shortcut-modifier and focus rules still rest on the Windows 7 guide (Q-39). Send those six if you want them checked too.

**Changed on Windows**
- **Settings:** a page in the window that applies each change at once, with no OK or Cancel, and named Settings, not Options. It is the last item of the sidebar or the toolbar's More menu, and About moves to the bottom of the Settings page. OK, Cancel and Apply stay only for a properties dialog of one object.
- **Menu bar:** now optional. Apps with many commands (editing apps) keep one; others may use a toolbar with a More menu, as long as every command is on one of them.
- **Dialogs:** a default button only when one answer is clearly likely and safe. The title is the question, with no caption naming the command. Order is main action, optional second action, then the safe button at the right end, and every dialog has a safe button.
- **Wording:** sentence case for everything, window and dialog titles included. The problem message is the app's ("We couldn't save your file"). "Select" replaces "click" in help text. Toolbar labels are preferably one word.
- **Context menus:** every command for the item, common ones first, and commands that don't apply are left out rather than disabled.
- **Labels and links:** field labels sit above the field. Links only navigate; actions are buttons, and every link's tooltip says where it leads.

**Now the same on both platforms:** no colon after labels; placeholders stay while the field is empty; radio buttons for two to five options; a mixed checkbox goes all on, then all off; a submit button may stay disabled if the required fields are marked; steppers stop at their limits. kvit-ui's Check and Stepper already behave this way.

**Removed from the Windows 7 forms:** the four-word toolbar labels, wrapping steppers, "a link may run a light command", disabled Cut and Copy in text menus, the Options dialog, About in the Help menu, and the colon on labels.

**Added:** one new rule, LAY-10, for in-app navigation (back history, breadcrumb, sidebar or top row). Badges inside the window, in-window notice bars and document tabs were folded into existing rules.

**Open questions:** 11 are now settled (Q-1, Q-2, Q-9, Q-22, Q-26, Q-27, Q-28, Q-29, Q-30, Q-32, Q-37) and five narrowed. The current guidance raised 12 new ones (Q-41 to Q-52), so 41 remain open. The one with the biggest cost is Q-41: Windows 11 lets apps put Back, search and tabs in the title bar, which would mean kvit-ui drawing its own title bar; I recommend keeping the system frame.

kvit-ui now enforces 20 rules, partly covers 101, contradicts 9 and doesn't cover 69. KEY-6 (the default button and Enter) moved from contradicts to partly, because a dialog without a default now suits Windows. The order of library work in `library-gaps.md` is unchanged, except that the toolbar is now built alongside the menu bar, and a Settings page and a teaching-tip component are added.
